title: C1551E — Powertrain control module (PCM) connector
introduction:
I use this reference as the powertrain controller’s address book: find a cavity in the drawing, then read its table row to learn which circuit belongs there. Sensor information, reference supplies, signal returns and actuator commands share the housing, but they have different jobs. Sharing an apartment building doesn’t make every resident an electrician.

Start with the connector identification, match the illustrated cavity label, and read across the assignment table. Keep any alternative rows together; a blank qualifier does not tell you which alternative applies to your vehicle. The drawing’s shading has no supplied legend, so use the table to establish the recorded assignment.

This page supports connector and circuit lookup. It does not establish physical viewing direction, access or disconnection steps, electrical test conditions, or replacement-wire selection. The gauge convention and the Size and Used codes are not explained here. The metadata and drawing also have an unresolved cavity-count discrepancy; do not fill in unpictured positions.

edits.why: I navigate the drawing by its printed cavity labels and housing outline. As displayed, the broad cavity bank is on the left and the narrower bank is on the right. Labels increase from left to right within each row, with higher-numbered rows above. These are page directions, not an established view from the wire side or mating side. The housing projections are visual landmarks; their release or locking functions are not identified.

Match the drawing label to Cavity, then read Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number across the same row. Circuit Number identifies the circuit record; Function describes its association with a sensor, supply, return or controlled device. A reference supply and a signal return are distinct connections, so I keep their roles separate even when they concern the same system. Preserve blank entries and alternative rows: differing color records or gauge and terminal combinations are not permission to choose a preferred version. Read the codes literally, and take the identified circuit into the applicable diagnostic instructions before making an electrical test or repair decision.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata states Pin Count 98, while the supplied illustration shows cavity labels 1–95. The evidence does not reconcile the difference; review is needed before presenting the illustration as a complete view matching that count.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 118 primary units, six complete pages/one figure and two edits. Original first CLI author covered 55 units/two headings. Public prose remains exactly equal to original author; count disagreement already disclosed. Original partial author remains separate; physical count and unqualified gauge/terminal alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
